land.text: Upper Egypt, which Horwennefer 'led ... in secession from the rule of Ptolemy IV Philopator in 205 BC'

predecessors.note: The state is the Theban rebel kingdom of two successive pharaohs, Horwennefer (205 to c.200) and Ankhwennefer (c.200 to c.186): one state, so one dossier, with the change of pharaoh as a rename. Cliopatria has only the Ankhwennefer row (-197..-171).

land.text: the Thebaid and the Aswan frontier, reconquered by Ptolemy V's army by c. 186 BC

successors.note: The page says the rebel army 'was decisively defeated' c. 186 BC; Many southern rebels were granted amnesties.

capitals.name: Thebes (Luxor)
capitals.note: 'both rebel pharaohs stressed their strong connections to Thebes'; the Ankhwennefer page calls Thebes the rebels' capital and says it was lost around his accession and finally taken by the Ptolemies in 191.

capitals.name: Syene (Aswan)
capitals.note: 'His last stronghold might have been Syene'; he 'retreated to the border of Kush'. A reading, not a dated move.

correction.text: Upper Egypt in secession from Thebes, 205 BC (Cliopatria's -197 shape borrowed for the earlier years)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 197 but Horwennefer 'led Upper Egypt in secession ... in 205 BC' and Ankhwennefer succeeded him by 201-199. The pages give no boundary, so the 197 shape is borrowed; the Ankhwennefer page says Thebes was lost 'either shortly before or after' his accession and that he had 'regained the Thebaid', so the true outline moved in 199-197 and is not recoverable from these pages.

176,124 km2 (Egypt, 23.4-27.6 N). The page has the Ptolemies retaking Lycopolis in 197 or 196 and, in 191, 'retaking Sauty province after heavy fighting, and capturing Thebes', so the shape stands to 192 and the new keyframe -191 takes over. The infobox gives no area to compare. Lycopolis is 'in the Delta' on the page, though Asyut (Lycopolis of Upper Egypt) lies at the shape's northern edge; the page is not clear which is meant.

correction.text: Syene and the border of Kush: after Thebes fell in 191 he 'retreated to the border of Kush'; 'His last stronghold might have been Syene'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the last five years: Thebes (25.7 N) and Sauty (Asyut) were taken in 191, so only the far south remained. The extent is the researcher's reading of 'retreated to the border of Kush' and 'last stronghold ... Syene'; Aswan province is the nearest named unit.

correction.text: use keyframe ankhwennefer_-191 (Aswan, the border of Kush) for -188 to -186; no shape after c. 186

keyframe_review.note: 110,283 km2 reaching 26.4 N, which still contains Thebes, yet the page has the Ptolemies capturing Thebes in 191. Cliopatria also runs to -171 while the page ends the kingdom c. 186 ('The war continued until c. 186 BC, when Ankhwennefer's Egyptian-Nubian army was decisively defeated'; infobox reign 201/200-187/186). Years -185..-171 should not be drawn.

ledger.note: 205: Horwennefer secedes in Upper Egypt, starting the Great Theban Revolt. The page says he 'led Upper Egypt in secession from the rule of Ptolemy IV Philopator in 205 BC'; the infobox reign is 206/205-201/200 and both rebel pharaohs 'stressed their strong connections to Thebes'. The page gives no boundary.

c. 200: Ankhwennefer succeeds Horwennefer as pharaoh of the Theban kingdom. 'Ankhwennefer succeeded Horwennefer as pharaoh in Upper Egypt between 201 and 199; the exact date remains unclear'; infobox reign 201/200-187/186. The Horwennefer page: 'He appears to have died before 197 BC'. Same state, new pharaoh; colour continues.

region.text: the rebel Thebaid between Aswan and Lycopolis

ledger.note: 197: the Ptolemies counter-attack. 'in 197 or 196 BC, the Ptolemies retook Lycopolis in the Delta' (the page doubts whether rebels held it); the war then runs south for six years. The ptolemaic-kingdom dossier dates the Asyut fighting 195-191 from another page.

191: Thebes falls. 'The Ptolemaic army advanced southward, retaking Sauty province after heavy fighting, and capturing Thebes in 191.' Ankhwennefer then 'retreated to the border of Kush' and 'managed to enlist Nubian troops'.

region.text: the far south, 'His last stronghold might have been Syene'

ledger.note: 186: the war ends. 'The war continued until c. 186 BC, when Ankhwennefer's Egyptian-Nubian army was decisively defeated.'

region.text: the last rebel-held land, Syene and the border of Kush

ledger.note: 186: the Theban kingdom ends. 'Ankhwennefer's son was killed in the fighting, but he was captured'; he 'was imprisoned, but might have been spared by Ptolemy V after Egyptian priests intervened on his behalf'; 'Many southern rebels were granted amnesties.' The infobox gives death c. 186.

wars.name: Great Theban Revolt

zones.text: Upper Egypt from Aswan to Lycopolis

wars.outcome: Ptolemaic victory c. 186: the Theban pharaohs' army, which had Nubian troops, was 'decisively defeated' and the south amnestied.
wars.note: The Horwennefer page headlines Horwennefer as 'Pharaoh in the Great Theban Revolt' and cites 'The Great Revolt of the Egyptians (205-186 BC)'; the 186 defeat and the 191 capture of Thebes are from the Ankhwennefer page. Kush is named as pressuring him and, after 191, as the border he retreated to; the page does not make Kush a belligerent on either side with certainty.

certainty.note: The pages name towns (Thebes, Lycopolis, Sauty, Syene), not a frontier; the Nile valley outline is approximate throughout.

notes: One state, two pharaohs: Horwennefer (205 to c.200) and Ankhwennefer (c.200 to c.186) held the same Theban kingdom, so the dossier starts in 205 (Horwennefer page) rather than at Cliopatria's 197 and ends c.186 rather than 171. Dates for the middle years are uncertain across pages: the Ankhwennefer page has Thebes lost 'either shortly before or after' his accession and 'regained' without a year; the ptolemaic-kingdom dossier (another agent, from the Ptolemaic Kingdom page) dates Thebes retaken December 199, the Thebaid regained c.197, Asyut fighting 195-191 and the final defeat 27 August 186 under Komanos. This dossier cites only the pages it opened and so keeps the 199-197 swing out of the ledger. Cliopatria's 110k km2 shape for 188-171 still contains Thebes and outlives the kingdom by fifteen years. Borrowed boundary: no page gives an outline, the -197 shape is used for 205-198. Lycopolis is 'in the Delta' on the page; Asyut is the Upper Egyptian Lycopolis and lies on the shape's northern edge. Kush: the page speaks of pressure from Kush and Nubian troops on his side; kingdom-of-kush is listed as a war party without a dated event. A state Cliopatria lacks that this one needs: none; Horwennefer is folded in here. The Ptolemaic reconquest of Lower Nubia in 186 is on the ptolemaic-kingdom dossier (gain from kingdom-of-kush), not here. Page budget: 2 pages opened plus the disambiguation page.
